posts.heading: October 22, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 22 species, with 19 heard and 10 seen, and 160 feeder visits, the fewest of any day in the past week and well below the week's average of 256.4. The species count sat above the average of 19.9, and 420 detections ran slightly above the week's average of 398.7. Seven species were both heard and seen, with Eastern Towhee leading the ear counts at 99 and Tufted Titmouse leading visits at 54.

Thirteen species were recorded on all seven days, including Carolina Chickadee, Northern Cardinal, Blue Jay, Carolina Wren and Tufted Titmouse, so the regulars held. Mourning Dove, recorded on six of the previous seven days, was not recorded today. Eastern Screech-Owl returned after 18 days away with one probable visual, and Northern Flicker returned after 10 days away with one detection.

White-throated Sparrow was heard for the first time at this station, with 21 detections, but the audio source was switched repeatedly across the week and again throughout today, from 07:17 to 23:56. Those switches among pi, c120 and pi-mic (movo-dom1) began on 10-16.

posts.heading: October 21, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 188 feeder visits and 18 species on the day, quieter than the prior week's average of 271.0 visits and 20.1 species. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 57, followed by Carolina Wren with 21 and Carolina Chickadee with 18. Fifteen species were heard and 11 were seen, with 8 of them detected both ways.

Heard detections totaled 312, below every other day in the past week, which ran from 390 to 426. Fourteen species were recorded on all seven days, including House Finch, Northern Cardinal and Tufted Titmouse, so the regulars held. Blue Grosbeak, Gray Catbird and Pileated Woodpecker, which appeared earlier in the week, were not recorded today.

The audio source changed many times on this day, including repeatedly in the early morning, so heard detections came from a mix of sources. The first visual was Northern Cardinal 16 min before sunrise and the last was Northern Cardinal 12 min after sunset.

posts.heading: October 20, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 22 species and 198 feeder visits, a busier day by species count than the past week's average of 19.9 but quieter at the feeder than its average of 272.6 visits. Tufted Titmouse led the visual counts with 48 confident visits, and Carolina Chickadee and Eastern Towhee led the audio detections with 74 and 72. Blue Jay, Carolina Wren, Northern Cardinal, and Carolina Chickadee were among the species recorded on all seven days of the past week, and the Eastern Bluebird returned after 11 days away, last recorded 2026-10-09.

White-throated Sparrow was seen at this station for the first time today, with one confident visual record. Gray Catbird, recorded on five of the past seven days, was not heard or seen today.

The audio source was changed many times across the past week, including repeatedly through this day, between the pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1), and c120 inputs.

posts.heading: October 19, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 190 feeder visits and 19 species, with 16 heard, 11 seen and 8 both. That was quieter than the past week's average of 295.9 visits and 20.4 species, though the 415 heard detections sat close to the 428.6 average. Only October 17, with 180 visits, had fewer visits in the past week.

All 14 species recorded across the past seven days were also recorded today. Tufted Titmice led the seen visits with 45, followed by House Finches and Carolina Chickadees with 24 each. Several species from the past week were absent today, including Canada Goose, American Kestrel, Brown-headed Cowbird, American Goldfinch and Barred Owl, and no species was heard here for the first time.

The audio source changed many times today, most often between pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1) and c120, including a switch to pi-mic at 07:14 and a run of changes from 18:32 through 19:09. Detections on this day therefore came from several microphones, so the heard counts reflect that mix rather than a single source.
